With virtuosic technique, heavy grooves and ancient melodies, he has created a sound all his own and become one of the leading pianists of his generation. Composed, arranged and orchestrated by Hamasyan himself, it brings folk melodies together with the energy of rock. Born in Gyumri, Armenia, in 1987, Hamasyan started playing piano at three. He won the piano competition at the Montreux Jazz Festival in 2003 and went on to take first prize at the Thelonious Monk International Jazz Piano Competition. Compañía Kaari & Roni Martinis an award-winning flamenco company based in Helsinki , rooted in the meeting point between flamenco and contemporary art. Bringing together members from many countries and cultures, the ensemble creates original, multidisciplinary stage works that resonate far beyond Finland. Now, for the first time in far too long, the Finnish flamenco phenomenon returns to Sweden. In ROOTS , musical traditions meet in a true melting pot: Arabic, Jewish and Romani music blend with flamenco rhythms and the bowed lyre, a traditional Finnish string instrument. Ali Saadbrings traditional Arabic song, Roni Martindraws on his family's Jewish musical heritage, Pekko Käppiadds Finnish folk music on the bowed lyre, and dancer Mariana Colladodrives the rhythm with flamenco dance. On stage you'll hear Finnish, Arabic, Hebrewand Ladino, but there's no need to understand the words. The music speaks for itself, and the performance is suitable for all ages. Sulaf is a Sudanese singer, oud player and composer who weaves together rhythm, Sufi poetry and folk traditions into a deeply personal musical expression. With her powerful voice and a soundscape where the oud meets subtle electronics, she creates music about loss, identity, longing and resilience. Her debut album ABA, made with French producer Maxime Kosinetz (Imarhan, Tinariwen), takes its starting point in Sufi poetry written by her great-grandfather. The project began during a short artist residency in Paris, but took on new meaning when the war in Sudan forced Sulaf into exile. The album follows that journey through longing, memory and spiritual resilience, in a sound that feels both ancient and strikingly contemporary. At the heart of Sulaf's music is her expressive voice, equally capable of intimate vulnerability and soaring intensity. She carries forward the legacy of Sudanese artists while exploring new musical paths that bring people and cultures together. His father was at first reluctant to see his son become a musician, so Vieux started out on drums and calabash and secretly took up the guitar in 2001. With the support of kora master Toumani Diabaté, he eventually won his father's blessing, and Ali appeared on Vieux's self-titled 2007 debut, one of his last studio recordings. Divanhana is one of the most internationally acclaimed bands from Bosnia and Herzegovina. Since forming in Sarajevo in 2009, the group has carried sevdalinka, or sevdah, the deeply emotional song tradition of Bosnia and Herzegovina, to audiences around the world. Founded by young musicians from the Sarajevo Music Academy, Divanhana has developed its own musical language rooted in traditional urban songs and the musical heritage of the Balkans. title: Heinali & Andriana-Yaroslava Saienko | Global Sounds Festival
page_text: Heinali & Andriana-Yaroslava Saienko | Global Sounds Festival Home 2026 2025 2024 About Contact us Home 2026 2025 2024 About Contact us More More child HEINALI & ANDRIANA-YAROSLAVA SAIENKO MEDIEVAL MYSTICISM MEETS UKRAINIAN FOLK SINGING AND MODULAR SYNTHS IN A HYPNOTIC, HAUNTING PERFORMANCE. What does medieval mysticism sound like through a Ukrainian voice of today? In Hildegard, Ukrainian duo Heinali and Andriana-Yaroslava Saienko take on two compositions by the German nun, mystic and composer Hildegard von Bingen (1098–1179), and bring them together with the Ukrainian singing tradition known as avtentyka. Avtentyka, literally “authentic,” is a movement within Ukrainian folk music that returns to older singing styles and vocal techniques. It is physical, raw and improvisational, far from the polished folk aesthetic of official Soviet culture. In Saienko’s hands, the voice becomes a living instrument that can stretch, crack, soar and fill a room. Heinali, the alias of sound artist and composer Oleh Shpudeiko, has long explored the meeting point between early European music and electronic sound. Gordiy Starukh is a musician, multi-instrumentalist, sound producer and instrument maker from Lviv. He is best known for his work with the kolisna lira, the Ukrainian hurdy-gurdy, and for bringing the instrument's distinctive sound into contemporary music. For Starukh, the hurdy-gurdy is more than an instrument. It carries centuries of Ukrainian history and is closely tied to the tradition of wandering musicians who passed songs, stories and cultural memory from generation to generation. Parts of this tradition were suppressed during the Soviet era, and Starukh has devoted much of his artistry to bringing its music and craft into our time. A trained sculptor, he builds the instruments he plays himself. He made his first hurdy-gurdy in 2009, developing his craft largely through experimentation, and today he is an internationally recognized instrument maker with more than 200 handmade instruments in the hands of musicians and collectors around the world. But Starukh isn't out to recreate the past.
